tokenizer_decision: The code-weighted 8k tokenizer shortens programs by 1.36% versus the current tokenizer, but only 0.28% versus the fresh balanced control. The 16k version shortens code by 3.17% and reduces over-limit programs from 278 to 219 of 15,304; at width512 its shared token table adds 4,194,304 parameters. The tested explicit Python boundaries lengthen programs by 16.34% and questions by 78.53%, so reject this particular boundary rule. All variants round-trip exactly with zero unknown tokens. Retain code8192 and code16384 as a matched vocabulary-size pair for a short future training test; compression does not establish an accuracy or wall-time gain. No tokenizer has replaced the best checkpoint.
consistency_decision: Among 503 sampled repeated questions with distinct original programs, 177 (35.19%) have at least two conflicting numeric results; 284 fully agree, 38 have insufficient executable results, and 4 have partial agreement. Five groups hit the eight-program cap. This supports investigating a cheap original-data filtering experiment, but gives no authority to choose a correct answer or create targets. No filtering has been applied.
